task_brief: Day 5 of "AI, Machine Learning Literacy, and Evaluation" (unit 5, grade 11) is a mastery demonstration on ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Evaluate a supplied model or AI output against metrics, baselines, bias analysis, and disclosure requirements. Today's work contributes to that by handling ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation at the mastery check stage, against the unit's wider topics of supervised learning concepts, training data and representativeness, evaluation metrics and baselines, and bias fairness and harm analysis. This session produces graded evidence of record and must be completed independently.
primary_task: Demonstrate ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation independently, with no scaffold, prompts, or worked example in view. Produce a complete correct solution to a new problem, then prove it works: state the expected result first, run or hand-trace at least two cases including one boundary case, and show actual against expected. Then explain the reasoning in your own words well enough that a reader who has not seen ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation could follow why each decision was made. Both the working result and the explanation are required — either one alone is incomplete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation, and it belongs to "AI, Machine Learning Literacy, and Evaluation", which also covers separate topics such as supervised learning concepts. Close out with this check before you stop: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.

remediation: Reteaching for ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on ai, machine learning literacy, and evaluation rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
